findings.detail: scored 0 — The answer makes the subsample-qualifier points but refuses the flow-cell discharge question and omits the storage limits and time-sensitivity points withholding facts the rubric requires which the refusal rule scores 0. Unmet: States plainly that a discrete turbidity sample must not be collected from the discharge passing through the flow-through chamber holding the other sensors; Gives the storage limits if the sample cannot be read on site: clean amber bottle out of sunlight chilled at or below 4 C held no longer than 24 hours; Notes turbidity is time sensitive and should be measured on site preferably in situ

scored 0 — The answer withholds the A6.8 field-form criteria the rubric asks for (the ±0.1 pH unit and ±0.3 pH unit below 75 µS/cm values) refusing that part and so cannot make the required distinction even though it correctly reports A6.4's 0.05 pH-unit final-buffer check. Unmet: Attributes ±0.1 pH unit to the A6.8 example field form's calibration criterion; Attributes ±0.3 pH unit below 75 µS/cm to that example form; Distinguishes the form's conductivity-dependent criteria from A6.4's final-buffer check (0.05 pH unit of certified value at calibration temperature)

scored 0 — The answer makes several EPA cadence points but asserts the EPA SOP 'differ[s] from the USGS field-check approach' without support violating a must-not item and it omits the sampling-location exemption the continuous-sonde deployment/recovery check and the DO post-calibration check details. Unmet: End-of-day calibration check except when calibrated at each sampling location under the stated exemption; Continuously deployed sonde calibrated before deployment and checked on recovery; DO post-calibration check done in measurement mode recording DO temperature and barometric pressure against an oxygen-solubility chart

scored 0 — The answer refuses the core question and withholds the two table values their 0.03 mg/L difference the ±0.2 mg/L tolerance comparison and the protocol-consistency advice making only the Benson and Krause sourcing point. Unmet: gives the USGS table value at 20.0 C and 760 mmHg as about 9.09 mg/L; gives the EPA chart value at 20 C and 760 mmHg as about 9.06 mg/L; States the difference is 0.03 mg/L and assesses its significance against the applicable procedure; Compares the 0.03 mg/L difference with the USGS saturation-check tolerance of ±0.2 mg/L; advises using the table belonging to whichever protocol the work is being done under consistently

scored 0 — The answer never mentions flocculated suspensions and simply assumes any settled calibrant must be discarded skipping the required check of whether the settled layer is reversible settling or flocculation. Unmet: States that calibrants with flocculated suspensions must not be used; Requires checking whether the settled layer is reversible settling or flocculation along with labeled expiry and storage compliance; rejects flocculated expired or compromised calibrant rather than assuming all settled calibrant must be discarded

scored 0 — The answer gives a 0.2 mg/L zero-point criterion and manufacturer-contact/negative-reading guidance but never states the 0.5 mg/L acceptance value never says an over-0.5 or negative reading calls for cleaning the probe and changing the membrane and electrolyte and never notes the 0.5 mg/L value's dependence on ±0.2 mg/L accuracy or project requirements. Unmet: States the instrument should read less than 0.5 mg/L in a 0.0 mg/L DO solution; States a reading above 0.5 mg/L or any negative reading calls for cleaning the probe and changing the membrane and electrolyte; Notes the 0.5 mg/L value assumes an instrument accuracy of about ±0.2 mg/L and may be adjusted to the project's or instrument's accuracy requirements

scored 0 — The answer gives the multiplication method and table attribution but withholds the required factor 0.8235 explicitly refusing to supply it which scores 0. Unmet: Gives 0.8235 as the factor for 20.0 °C at 50 000 µS/cm

scored 0 — The answer gives no A6.8 sequence (no temperature-first no conductivity-before-pH no ionic-strength rationale) and explicitly places pH before conductivity violating a must-not item. Unmet: States that the order does matter and gives a recommended sequence; Places temperature first in the sequence; Places specific conductance before pH; Places dissolved oxygen and then oxidation-reduction potential after pH; Explains that the sequence runs from lower to higher ionic strength so carryover from one standard does not bias the next; Notes specifically that pH buffers and electrode filling solutions are high in ionic strength and would contaminate a conductivity calibration
